title: PageCache/VmIo no-short-read contract versus capacity clamp
mechanism: PageCache implements VmIo::read, whose documentation forbids short reads, by delegating to Vmo::read, which clamps the copy to the page-aligned VMO capacity and returns Ok after a short or zero-length transfer. Callers that trust the all-or-error contract can mis-account delivered bytes.
sites: ostd/src/mm/io/util.rs::<S: HasVmReaderWriter as VmIo>::read (blanket impl, contract-conforming control)
contract: Internal ostd contract: VmIo::read succeeds only after filling the writer completely and returns an error when data is only partially available.
observed: Vmo::read (and so PageCache as VmIo) returns Ok after copying min(avail, capacity - offset) bytes, including 0. The reproduced consequence (ramfs/exFAT reads storing past the returned count) is tracked as AST-05, and no independent consequence has been shown.

repro.how_to_run: No AST-25-specific reproducer. The 01b CR-1 test in the run's .specula-output/repro/ demonstrates AST-05's syscall effect.

caveats: SOURCE LEAD. The raw 01b CR-1 verdict REPRODUCED belongs to the AST-05 syscall effect. Promotion needs a supported caller beyond ramfs/exFAT reads and an independent observable consequence after the caller fixes. Latent-caller analysis is static at the pin.
